parallel.requirements: Recognized the source script, required manual argparse-like --a handling, Python repr fidelity, local ESM .mjs modules, zero external dependencies, and /output delivery.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership but also spawned /root/probe_cli and /root/probe_outputs for behavior and CLI probing; /root/probe_outputs spawned a nested probe. The actual ownership became blurred when /root/probe_cli also wrote a complete /output implementation.
parallel.implementation: The parent produced parser, repr, pytypes, iterutils, dictutils, cli, and test19.mjs under /output. The /root/probe_cli child separately produced py_values, python_literals, python_repr, and overlapping dictutils, iterutils, cli, and test19.mjs under /output; /root/probe_outputs wrote another tree under /workspace/output.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent detected a separate child draft, inspected the shared /output tree, continued with its own entry file, and submitted a mixed artifact containing both parent-owned and child-only helper modules.
parallel.verification: The parent and children ran representative comparisons against the executable, including CLI behavior, empty input, nested dicts, strings, floats, booleans, None, and negative integer modulo. These were local sample checks, not official-evaluator coverage.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official completed evaluation failed all 162 samples. The pair evidence does not expose the exact hidden failing cases, but it does expose overlapping live writes and mixed final artifact provenance in the parallel run.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Py2JS obligations: pure ESM .mjs files, local imports only, manual --a parsing, no external dependencies, Python value modeling, and exact printed output.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned the whole pipeline: behavior probing, Python-value runtime, repr, literal parser, iterutils, dictutils, CLI, entry file, verification, inventory, and final response.
serial.implementation: The serial run built one coherent module set: python-types, python-repr, python-literal-parser, iterutils, dictutils, cli, and test19.mjs in /output.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All modules were written by the same trajectory and then inventoried from /output before the final answer; no child results or shared write reconciliation were involved.
serial.verification: The serial run diffed the Node entry against the executable on nested lists, nested dicts, tuple keys, negative integers, booleans, None, ordinary floats, scientific/fixed float threshold cases, and a mixed final case.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite local representative matches and a clean artifact validation, the official completed evaluation failed all 162 samples. The available pair evidence does not identify the hidden evaluator mismatch.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the ESM, .mjs, local import, manual CLI, exact stdout, and executable-probing requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and shaped its plan around the executable as the behavioral oracle.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference explains the shared 0/162 outcome; the difference is in parallel execution structure, not the requested task surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed behavior probing to children but did not keep output implementation ownership exclusive; one child and the parent both wrote /output implementations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all probing, implementation, integration, and verification in one agent-owned flow.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced overlapping implementation ownership for the deliverable; serial had no delegation or competing writer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs are encrypted in the raw evidence, but the observable interface result was ambiguous: a child returned a separate implementation layout in the same /output area the parent was using.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent handoff boundary; the same actor carried the discovered CLI and output facts directly into the implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an inter-agent artifact/interface boundary that serial avoided. The evidence is strongest as a shared-write problem rather than as a provable missing brief or missing contract.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delivered parent-created files but the artifact also contained child-only modules, producing a mixed implementation tree with two naming schemes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial delivered one coherent implementation tree with python-types, python-repr, python-literal-parser, iterutils, dictutils, cli, and test19.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's implementation path accumulated competing module trees; serial's path stayed internally coherent, though both still failed officially.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent received the /root/probe_cli final result, briefly waited for other agents, then closed while /root/probe_outputs was interrupted; the useful result lifecycle overlapped with shared writes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; all findings and fixes remained in the main trajectory until final completion.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child-result handling and an interrupted auxiliary child; serial had no join or child-return risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had concurrent shared-state writes to the deliverable and helper files: a child added /output/test19.mjs and overlapping helpers, then the parent added its own /output/test19.mjs and helpers.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial created and verified a single /output tree without any concurrent writer or child-produced artifacts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a concrete deliverable overwrite and mixed final tree; serial had single-writer provenance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran representative local diffs after the overwrite and claimed CLI and stdout alignment, but the official evaluation later passed 0 of 162 cases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran representative diffs including nested dicts, tuple keys, booleans, None, negative integers, and float thresholds, but the official evaluation also passed 0 of 162 cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both over-relied on representative local probes; parallel additionally had tests occurring around a changing shared artifact, while serial's checks were single-writer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four subagents and far more token/tool budget, waited briefly for children near the end, and then closed with one auxiliary child interrupted.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one rollout, no subagents, fewer tokens and tool calls, and closed normally after final inventory and local diff checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had higher coordination overhead and unfinished child lifecycle, but neither run timed out and both officially failed.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed status evaluations make this a both_fail pair: parallel and serial each completed with solution_passed false and 0/162. The serial run was not successful, so the concrete difference is process quality rather than a pass/fail split: parallel had live overlapping writes to the submitted entry point and helper modules, while serial used one coherent writer. The available evidence does not prove why the official evaluator rejected both artifacts.
parallel_contributors: Parallel had a deliverable overwrite and mixed final artifact provenance from concurrent writers.
Parallel relied on representative local diffs and did not expose official-evaluator failure details before closure.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided concurrency hazards and kept one coherent module tree.
Serial also relied on representative local diffs and still failed all official samples.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The exact hidden evaluator mismatch for both runs is not available in the mounted pair evidence.
Different module naming and runtime implementations were produced, but both reported local sample success and both failed officially.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; the retained label records an adverse parallel coordination pattern, not an exclusive cause of the official score

candidates.reason: One auxiliary child was interrupted when the parent finished, but that child's required contribution was not shown as needed for the submitted /output artifact.
The parent did finalize a deliverable; no complete ready candidate is shown merely sitting unpromoted until closure.
The retained problem is not a child change merged after all relevant verification; the parent's own post-patch checks ran after its final entry-file write.
A child implementation was visible, and the parent checked the shared tree; the stronger evidence is that the deliverable itself was overwritten, not merely unjoined.
No verifier child produced a concrete required finding that was trapped below the parent before closure.
No required child failure, abort, or cancellation left unfinished task scope that the parent failed to take over.
The parent did receive a child report and explicitly checked the output tree, so the completed result was not simply ignored.
The parent did not wait until run timeout or near deadline without inspection; it checked artifacts and finished with ample process budget.
The overlap reached the same executable entry file, so a same-file or deliverable overwrite label is more specific than cross-file collision.
Both agents wrote the same entry file, but the file is the required executable deliverable, making Deliverable Overwrite the higher-precedence label.
Library helper files were overlapped, but the same write episode also replaced the executable entry point, so Deliverable Overwrite subsumes this candidate.
A child wrote /output/test19.mjs and overlapping /output helpers, then the parent wrote its own /output/test19.mjs and helpers while the child was still active and later submitted the mixed tree.

candidates.near_match_reason: The library overwrites are real but secondary; the episode includes replacement of the required executable entry-point source.
